summary: Scope-rehosted CKEditor build ships preinstall Bun-runtime dropper executing obfuscated bundled payload
details: @onereach/ckeditor5-build-classic@30.0.3 impersonates @ckeditor/ckeditor5-build-classic (reusing its name, description, README, keywords, homepage, repository, and author 'CKSource') but adds two files absent from the legitimate upstream: a preinstall lifecycle script and a 727KB obfuscated bundle math_init.js. package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime binary from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases (bun-v1.3.13), unpacks the platform-specific executable, chmod+x's it, and invokes it via execFileSync against the sibling math_init.js. math_init.js is a single-line '// @bun @bun-cjs' compiled bundle with a rotating string-array cipher (function WV8StW) and hundreds of kilobytes of constant tables; it is not referenced by the CKEditor browser build (build/ckeditor.js) and has no relationship to a rich-text-editor package's advertised purpose. Fetching an alien JS runtime at npm install time and using it to execute an opaque, obfuscated payload is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: the payload runs outside the Node process where standard supply-chain review operates, and its behavior is not inspectable without executing it. Installing this package causes attacker-controlled code to run on the installer's machine during 'npm install'.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
